title: Who decides what happened first?

data.source: Rideout and Sorkin, classical sequential growth dynamics for causal sets (1999). Compared in a seeded toy: populations of R4 rotors and of memoryless cutters, 200,000 runs each, and one 20-cut order with signals.

prediction: As given, the cuts of separate loops are unordered, so CRR alone grows no joined order. If clock time is taken as the order of births, regular threshold cutters break Rideout and Sorkin's covariance and Bell causality, and memoryless cutters keep them. With signals added, there are many "nows". And nothing in the finished order records whether it was grown.
baseline: Classical sequential growth for causal sets (Rideout and Sorkin 1999), with transitive percolation as its simplest law and memoryless cutters as a decoy.
why: Not every prediction held: P5_many_nows. The growing-block reading is ONTOLOGY in Phoenix and stays undecided: the order is the same however it is built. What is shared with causal sets: local events and a partial order once signals are added. What is left over: causal sets have a growth law that needs no clock; CRR has clocks and no growth law between loops.

forks.no birth order, no signals (CRR as given: separate chains; the growth conditions have nothing to act on
forks.clock birth order, no signals: covariance and Bell causality fail for rotors, hold for memoryless cutters
forks.no birth order, signals (variant): a causal order with many nows; no growth law is given
forks.clock birth order, signals (variant): not run; the clock order already fails without signals

weighs: No outcome of this check could favour a growing block over a static one: the three builds are identical by construction.
result: Transitive percolation gave the same probability for two birth orders (0.050421 and 0.050421). Memoryless cutters gave ABA and AAB in the ratio 1.014; CRR rotors, whose gaps vary by only 0.216 of their mean, gave 16.23. With a spectator loop, the ratio of "A next" to "B next" moved by 0.008 for memoryless cutters and by 0.506 for rotors. In the variant with signals, 20 cuts had 16 "nows", 88 possible "blocks so far" against the 21 a single clock passes through, and 6317248 orders of becoming. Built three ways, the order was identical. One prediction of mine missed: I wrote that there would be more than 21 nows. There were 16: more than one, far fewer than I said.

framework.name: Causal set theory: classical sequential growth

precise_core: Causal sets and the growth conditions are defined exactly; the family of solutions is a theorem.
proved_by_others: A small community, with results on percolation limits by outside mathematicians (Brightwell and Georgiou).
differing_prediction: Sorkin's heuristic forecast of a small fluctuating cosmological constant of the observed order; Lorentz-invariant "swerves".
tested: The constant was measured in 1998. Detailed "everpresent Lambda" models have been set against cosmological data.
passed: The order of magnitude matched. The argument is heuristic and the detailed models are disputed.
replicated: The measurement is well replicated. The link from it to causal sets is not an independent result.
admits_open_problems: Its reviews say plainly that the quantum dynamics is unknown and that most large orders do not look like spacetime.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.
